patronOf.en-US: Apostles of the Slavs, patrons of Europe
patronOf.pt-BR: Apóstolos dos eslavos, padroeiros da Europa

prayerExcerpt.en-US: These are holy men who became friends of God, glorious heralds of divine truth.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Estes são homens santos, que se tornaram amigos de Deus, gloriosos arautos da verdade divina.

meta.face: Cyril (left): a thin, pale, scholarly man of about forty with an inverted-triangle face — a tall, broad forehead under the monastic hood narrowing sharply to the chin; a long, slender, slightly hooked nose; large, dark, prominent, intelligent eyes under straight black brows; smooth, flat cheeks; a small, thin mouth; a long, narrow black beard and a calm, inward gaze. Methodius (right): a man of about sixty with a broad, heavy, trapezoid face, wider at the jaw than at the brow — a large nose with a broad, fleshy, rounded tip; small, kind eyes creased at the corners under heavy dark eyebrows; full cheeks; a heavy jaw under the beard; a full mouth; a long, full iron-grey beard with darker streaks and a kindly, fatherly gaze. Methodius's beard is grey, not white.
meta.basis: Eastern and Western tradition (the 1848 Troyan Monastery fresco by Zahari Zograf, Matejko's 1885 painting) shows the younger Cyril with a dark beard and the elder Methodius with a grey or white one; Methodius was the elder brother, and Cyril, the monk, died at about forty-two in Rome in 869.
